title: Ad serving
like: ad auctions on a news site
brief: Each page view asks you to pick the best ad in about a quarter of a second: check who is allowed to see what, score the candidates with a model, run a quick auction and answer. Every impression and click must be counted exactly because money depends on it.

clarify.a: About 250 ms from the page asking to the ad being chosen, counting the trip from far-away readers (approx.). A slower answer means a blank space, which earns nothing.

clarify.q: What if the scoring model is slow?
clarify.a: Fall back to a simpler ranking. A decent ad on time beats a perfect ad too late.

clarify.q: Do we need the person's permission?
clarify.a: Yes. Personalised ads need consent. Check it on every request.

clarify.q: How exact must billing counts be?
clarify.a: Very. Lose no more than a minute of events, and never count one twice.

notes: Model scoring takes about 20 ms per ad request (approx.).
Impressions and clicks are billing records.

numbers.label: Ad requests per second at peak
Impression and click events per second
Campaign data in memory
numbers.how: 2 million live campaigns × 10 KB ≈ 20 GB, kept in cache (approx.)

hints: You have about a quarter of a second. Which steps must happen in that time, and which can happen afterwards?
Cache campaign data in memory, keep scoring in a model server, and send billing events down a stream so they are never lost and never slow the auction.
Budget freshness alone does not prevent concurrent overspend. Measure the failed boundary, waiting time and retry work before choosing a change.

editorial.summary: The auction is a tight loop of in-memory lookups and one fast model call. Everything that is not needed to choose the ad, such as counting, billing and reports, happens afterwards through a stream. A slow model must degrade the ad quality, not the page.

designs.name: Cache, score, auction, then stream
designs.why: Servers read campaigns from cache, fetch user features, and score with the model through a circuit breaker that gives up after 50 ms, so a slow model costs a few ads, not the page. Consent is checked each time. Events flow through a stream with three copies, so a minute of billing data is safe.

tradeoffs: A bigger model picks better ads but takes longer and costs more. A smaller one on time earns more than a perfect one late.
Longer cache times for campaign data save money but let a paused campaign keep showing for a minute.
Billing events go through a stream to be exact and safe, at the price of results appearing minutes later.
Consent checks add a lookup to every request, but showing ads without permission is far costlier.
editorial.realWorld: Real ad exchanges decide in about 100 ms and may handle millions of requests a second across all participants. A single site may see tens of thousands a second (approx.).

correctness.prompt: Ad serving: which invariant does this trace protect, and what failure would break it?
correctness.discussion: Bound auction latency and account for billable events exactly once. An auction needs a bounded decision window and explicit late-bid treatment. Transport deliveries are not independent billable actions. Budget freshness alone does not prevent concurrent overspend.

fields.label: Step 1. A bidder misses the auction deadline. What happens?
options: Exclude the late bid under the declared auction rule
Hold the page indefinitely for the highest possible bid
fields.explanation: An auction needs a bounded decision window and explicit late-bid treatment.

fields.label: Step 2. Click C is delivered twice after a retry. What is billed?
options: One billable event under a durable event identity and fraud policy
Two charges because two requests arrived
fields.explanation: Transport deliveries are not independent billable actions.

fields.label: Step 3. Budget is almost exhausted and two auctions reserve spend. What prevents excess?
options: Read the remaining cached budget in each auction
Atomic reservation with settlement and release states, or explicitly bounded overspend
fields.explanation: Budget freshness alone does not prevent concurrent overspend.

correctness.responsibility: Bound auction latency and account for billable events exactly once.
correctness.limits: The traffic model does not execute this protocol. The checked trace covers its central responsibility; the written explanation is retained for review.
